confidence_reason: The Mandate text and the two main Federal Register notices were read and match the summary. The stage sits at the low edge of implemented because the RFRA rule, delegations, HIPAA guidance withdrawal and any enforcement or funding actions were not found or not verified.

durability.why: Guidance rescissions, reorganizations and enforcement posture can be reversed quickly by a later administration; only a final rule or statute would be more durable.

est_completion.basis: Posture and guidance changes are largely in place; a final RFRA rule would need notice and comment (typically 12 to 24 months) and statutory changes would need Congress.

history.note: Red-team check found nothing that undercuts the status.

proposal: The Mandate recommends that OCR return to Trump-era enforcement of federal conscience laws, restore the Conscience and Religious Freedom Division with proper delegations, finalize a draft RFRA rule, restore religious exemption waivers for faith-based child welfare agencies, rescind legal analyses on the University of Vermont Medical Center case and California Weldon funding, and withdraw OCR's pharmacy abortion-drug guidance and June 2022 HIPAA guidance.

evidence.note: Reports HHS OCR sent letters on 2026-03-18 opening Weldon Amendment investigations of 13 states (California, Colorado, Delaware, Illinois, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Oregon, Vermont, Washington) over laws requiring insurance coverage of abortion; no violation finding or funding action yet; OCR says it would first seek informal resolution, then withhold funds or refer to DOJ.

redteam.note: An enforcement step the record had not found is now documented (Weldon investigations of 13 states opened 2026-03-18), though no finding or funding action followed in the source read.

review.mandate_note: Pages 492 to 494 ask HHS to move conscience and RFRA enforcement back from OGC to OCR, rescind the UVMMC and California Weldon analyses, fund and delegate authority to the Conscience and Religious Freedom Division, finalize the draft RFRA rule, restore child welfare waivers, and cut funds to violators; pages 496 and 497 ask OCR to withdraw its pharmacy guidance and the June 2022 HIPAA guidance.

source_checks.note: Confirms the 2026-01-26 notice (91 FR 3207, effective on publication) repudiating the July 2021 UVMMC letter, three November 2021 foster care RFRA letters, the August 2021 California Weldon letter, and December 2021 COVID-19 vaccine equity guidance; it does not mention HIPAA guidance or OGC memos.

Confirms the OCR organization notice (91 FR 39626), approved 2026-05-14 and effective 2026-06-28, with a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division under a Deputy Director enforcing Church, Coats-Snowe, Weldon and ACA 1303(b)(4) and 1553; RFRA and new delegations are not mentioned.

significance.rationale: Restoring conscience enforcement and withdrawing related guidance affects health workers with objections and some patients.

status_summary: On 2026-01-26 OCR published a notice rescinding or disavowing four sets of earlier documents: a 2021 letter withdrawing the University of Vermont Medical Center Church Amendments violation notice, three 2021 RFRA letters on foster care grant exemptions, a 2021 letter withdrawing the California Weldon Amendment violation notice, and 2021 COVID-19 vaccine equity guidance. On 2026-01-27 OCR rescinded its September 2023 retail pharmacy civil rights guidance. OCR's organization notice (approved 2026-05-14, effective 2026-06-28) lists a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division headed by a Deputy Director, naming the Church, Coats-Snowe and Weldon amendments and ACA sections 1303(b)(4) and 1553, but it does not mention RFRA or list new delegations. Not found in the sources reached: a final RFRA rule, withdrawal of the June 2022 HIPAA guidance, passage of the Conscience Protection Act, or funding terminations tied to Weldon findings.

timeline.event: OCR publishes a notice rescinding or disavowing four sets of earlier documents under Executive Order 14192 (University of Vermont Medical Center letter, three RFRA foster care letters, California Weldon letter, COVID-19 vaccine equity guidance).

OCR rescinds its September 29, 2023 retail pharmacy civil rights guidance, effective on publication; the abstract says the 2023 guidance had revised a 2022 guidance on reproductive health care access at pharmacies.
HHS modifies OCR's Privacy Act system of records to add records on complaints and reviews involving civil rights, conscience, religious freedom and health information privacy.

HHS OCR sent letters to 13 states opening Weldon Amendment investigations into state laws requiring insurance plans to cover abortion; as of the 2026-03-19 report no violation finding or funding action had occurred.

Federal Register publishes OCR's organization notice (approved 2026-05-14, effective 2026-06-28) describing a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division that runs OCR's national conscience and religious freedom enforcement program.

title: Restore OCR conscience enforcement and rescind Biden-era conscience and pharmacy guidance
uncertainties: All four sources are Federal Register notices I opened or saw in query results; I could not confirm enforcement activity (investigations, findings, funding actions), a RFRA rule, HIPAA guidance withdrawal or OGC memo rescission, partly because my web search quota ran out. The organization notice does not say whether the division was newly established or restored, and it replaced a strategic planning division in OCR's structure. The pharmacy rescission abstract states the 2023 guidance had revised a 2022 guidance; whether the 2022 guidance the Mandate cites remains posted was not checked. Whether the Mandate's 'immediate' items (rescind OGC legal analyses) were done beyond the four OCR documents is unknown.
